memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If anyone becomes aware that they are guilty—if they unwittingly touch anything ceremonially unclean (whether the carcass of an unclean animal, wild or domestic, or of any unclean creature that moves along the ground) and they are unaware that they have become unclean, but then they come to realise their guilt.'" - Lev 5:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a case of contamination the person did not choose and did not notice. They touched something unclean. They were unaware. And then, at some point, they realised.

Two things are worth understanding here. First, ceremonial uncleanness in Leviticus is not the same as moral wickedness. It was a system of pictures, teaching Israel about holiness, separation, and the reality of death in a fallen world. Touching a dead animal did not make someone wicked; it made them temporarily unfit to approach the sanctuary.

Second — and this is the enduring point — God took seriously the fact that we are affected by things we never chose.

That is honest about human life. We absorb attitudes from our culture without deciding to. We pick up cynicism, greed, or prejudice from the air around us. We are shaped by families and workplaces in ways we cannot see until much later.

The remedy is not paranoia. It is the moment described here: they come to realise. God brings things to light in His time, and when He does, there is provision.

These specific ceremonial laws are not binding on believers today; Christ has dealt with the whole system (Col 2:16-17). But the pattern of God graciously revealing what we could not see in ourselves — that continues.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I absorbed from my surroundings without ever choosing it?
2. Am I open to God showing me things about myself that I cannot currently see?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, show me what I have picked up without noticing. Cleanse what I could never have cleaned myself. Amen.
